what_happened: Verified by diffing grep -lE results under the old CANDIDATE_PATTERN vs. the proposed new open()-on-state.json limb across the full agent-system/extensions tree: the new limb introduces zero new candidate matches live, so the lint extension needs zero new EXCLUDED_FILES entries and cannot regress gate 12 on the current tree.

Read the originating issue-log entry (iss_1792068891206_SuioJu) directly rather than relying on the dispatch's paraphrase: the actual incident was an ad hoc, in-session Python json.dump invocation that never existed as a file under agent-system/extensions. This settles the required content-lint-vs-write-time-guard research question with direct evidence: a content lint cannot have stopped (and cannot stop a repeat of) the actual incident shape, since it only scans committed files; a write-time Bash PreToolUse hook is also warranted.

Found an always-permissionDecision:allow PreToolUse Write-matcher hook stub (matches on file_path containing 'state.json', labeled 'State file write') in agent-system/extensions/core/root-files/settings.json that does not exist anywhere in merge-sources/settings-hooks.json or any other extension source. It currently enforces nothing (unconditional allow) and appears unrelated/vestigial. Not investigated further or fixed -- out of scope for this task; flagged for a future cleanup task.

Research measured 'zero new EXCLUDED_FILES entries needed', which is true of the tree as it stands but not of the tree this work produces: the new shared pattern library holds the detection regex and the new hook's both-polarity test feeds the bad shape as synthetic fixture command strings, so both will trip the extended lint on their own text. The plan adds an inline-reasoned EXCLUDED_FILES entry in each creating phase (Phase 1 for the library, Phase 4 for the hook test), mirroring the existing self-exclusion entries for the lint and test-validate-task-creation-audit.sh.

The research report arrived with the detection predicate already prototyped against literal fixture lines, the zero-false-positive result measured by diffing grep result sets rather than asserted, and the content-lint-vs-write-time-guard question settled from the originating incident's actual shape. Planning needed only phase decomposition and the self-exclusion catch above, not any re-derivation of the predicate or re-measurement.

Phase 2's Scope Hypothesis assumed 3 literature-extension Python JSON writers. A plain recursive grep over agent-system/extensions/literature found 10 tracked script files (matching enumeration), but also transiently swept in 24+ vendored third-party package files from the extension's own gitignored, environment-local venv (scripts/literature-pyenv/venv/), since a plain grep is gitignore-unaware while the interactive shell's grep wrapper is. Fixed by enumerating via 'git grep' (tracked files only) instead of a plain recursive grep, which deterministically yields the 10 real source files regardless of whether the local venv happens to be bootstrapped in a given environment.

The new scripts/tests/test-validate-no-python-state-write.sh was created without the executable bit (chmod +x), unlike its sibling test-lint-state-writer-boundary.sh. run-all.sh --only correctly caught this as a SKIP ('not executable (exec-bit regression?)') rather than silently passing. Fixed by chmod +x on the source-store file and redeploying; re-ran run-all.sh --only to confirm both suites now PASS.
